title: Does removing semantic bearings make Jev's terminal-stage navigation worse?
question: The coffee run showed no difference without semantic bearings. The terminal stage asks Jev to choose among four destinations by distance and direction: does it navigate that stage worse when told signed degrees?
hypothesis: Removing semantic_bearings (and nothing else) does not change how Jev reaches and locks the four terminals: time to lock all four changes by less than 20 s, with no extra rejected or wasted decisions.

motivation.observation: semantic-bearings-navigation (5 paired live coffee runs): every run chose the same intents in the same order with and without the assist, and the assist passes its probes 20/20 without help. The coffee run exercises only two navigation choices; the terminal stage, with four destinations, is where directions could matter.

successCriteria: no-bearings locks all four terminals as reliably as full, within 20 s: with the probes, enough to retire semantic_bearings from the default question
falsificationCriteria: no-bearings is more than 20 s slower (median paired) or fails runs that full completes: keep the assist
limitations: Live, about 130 requests per run (≈ 1,300 for the experiment).
Five pairs can show a large effect; they cannot rule out a small one.
